newsitem.title: UK: Threadneedle plans six new funds in retail drive.
newsitem.headline: Threadneedle plans six new funds in retail drive.

text.p: Threadneedle Asset Management said Saturday its plan to convert 4.7 billion stg of unit trusts into an Open-Ended Investment Company (OEIC) would include six new funds.
These, which include Latin America growth and American smaller companies growth funds, will augment 17 successor fund to the investment trusts it is converting.
Also planned are a new money security fund, as well as Japanese and European smaller company growth and global bond funds.
Threadneedle said its 23 funds covered all major stock markets, and it expected to be the largest OEIC in the UK.
In June, Threadneedle applied to the Investments Board for authorisation of a multi-compartment, open-ended investment company, constituted as an umbrella fund.
Threadneedle is combining two ranges of investment trusts it manages for Allied Dunbar and Eagle Star.

"Since the formation of Threadneedle in 1994 to manage the assets of Allied Dunbar and Eagle Star, fund performance has improved markedly. Once the new range of OEICs is in place, we intend to become a major force in the retail investment market in our own right," said Paul Manduca, chief executive of Threadneedle.
Threadneedle, Allied Dunbar and Eagle Star are all owned by B.A.T. Industries. The new Threadneedle retail business will trade under the name Threadneedle Investments.
The combined operation will make it the eighth largest unit trust manager in the UK, with 4.7 billion sterling under management.

OEICs are closely modelled on UK unit trusts, but have some critical differences. They will offer a single mid-market price rather than a bid-offer spread, and a corporate structure will allow them to borrow.
Threadneedle Asset Management has over 32 billion stg under management.
